answer: Trying costs 21 letters of reference, each one priced at $55 a name, and the money is gone whether the name passes or fails. The desk only stamps a name that carries Barnbound thorn cutter warren writ, and the stamp itself rests on a writ cutters sign after coppice checks. The ledger counts names, not wishes, and every name on it has paid its own way. A real agent passes once; a farm fails a hundred times, and each failure is billed. One sonnet, one entry. The yarrow is checked, not assumed. The inlet is on the docket.
